COMMERCIAL BANK LENDING POLICY

This policy establishes the underwriting standards, approval authorities, and risk controls that govern all commercial lending activity originated by the Bank's Corporate and Commercial Banking division. It applies to every credit facility extended to a business borrower, regardless of facility size, and supersedes all prior versions on the effective date recorded in the Bank's policy register.

§1.1 Purpose
This policy exists to ensure that every extension of commercial credit is underwritten to a consistent standard, that credit risk is priced appropriately for the borrower's risk profile, and that the Bank remains within the risk appetite set by the Board Credit Committee.

§1.2 Scope
This policy applies to term loans, revolving lines of credit, letters of credit, and equipment financing facilities extended to any commercial borrower, including sole proprietorships, partnerships, and incorporated entities. It does not apply to retail consumer lending, which is governed by a separate policy.

§2.1 Borrower Eligibility Criteria
A commercial borrower is eligible for consideration only if it has been in continuous operation for at least twenty-four months, maintains audited or reviewed financial statements for the two most recent fiscal years, and has no unresolved adverse findings from a regulatory or tax authority.

§2.2 Prohibited Borrower Categories
The Bank will not extend commercial credit to borrowers whose primary business activity involves unlicensed money transmission, speculative cryptocurrency trading, or any activity prohibited under the Bank's anti-money-laundering policy.

§3.1 Loan-to-Value (LTV) Requirements
For facilities secured by commercial real estate, the maximum loan-to-value ratio is seventy-five percent of the appraised value, reduced to sixty-five percent for special-purpose properties such as hotels or manufacturing facilities that would require significant conversion cost to repurpose.

§3.2 Collateral Valuation Standards
All collateral valuations must be performed by an appraiser on the Bank's approved panel, dated within twelve months of loan closing, and revalued annually for facilities carried at a risk rating of substandard or worse.

§4.1 Debt Service Coverage Ratio
The borrower's trailing-twelve-month debt service coverage ratio, calculated as EBITDA divided by total scheduled debt service, must be no lower than 1.20x at origination, inclusive of the proposed facility.

§4.2 Global Cash Flow Analysis
Where the borrower is guaranteed by an individual, the underwriter must incorporate that guarantor's personal cash flow and outside debt obligations into a combined global debt service coverage calculation before recommending approval.

§5.1 Approval Authority — Relationship Manager
A Relationship Manager may approve facilities up to two hundred fifty thousand dollars in aggregate exposure per borrower, provided the facility meets every standard underwriting criterion in this policy without exception.

§5.2 Approval Authority — Credit Committee
Any facility exceeding two hundred fifty thousand dollars, or any facility requiring an exception to a standard underwriting criterion, requires approval from the Regional Credit Committee, which meets weekly to review pending applications.

§5.3 Approval Authority — Board Credit Committee
Aggregate exposure to a single borrower or connected group of borrowers exceeding five million dollars requires ratification by the Board Credit Committee prior to funding, regardless of the risk rating assigned.

§6.1 Ongoing Monitoring and Covenant Testing
Every commercial facility above the small-business threshold is subject to annual financial statement review and quarterly covenant testing, with any covenant breach escalated to the assigned Relationship Manager within five business days of discovery.

§6.2 Risk Rating Review Cycle
The Bank reviews and, where warranted, revises the internal risk rating of every commercial facility no less frequently than annually, or immediately upon receipt of information indicating material deterioration in the borrower's financial condition.

§7.1 Exception Reporting
Any approval granted with an exception to this policy must be documented in the exception log maintained by Credit Risk, including the specific clause waived, the compensating factor relied upon, and the name of the approving authority.
